about: CaseClerk demo video, locked cut A (2026-10-26). camNote: cam: [film time, scale, x, y, move seconds]; the source pixel (px,py) lands at (x + scale*px, y + scale*py). Moves ease power2.inOut; 0 s is a cut. A shot's "window" keys [film time, top, right, bottom, left, move seconds] crop the footage to the rest of the frame (insets in px); the crop resets when the shot ends. A dissolve between two case pages holds one zoom (the owner, #543): rsl-asked takes vpy's opening framing; approve takes vpy-evidence's 1.1x; vab opens on approve's framing and pushes in after N14; judge opens on vab's and then pushes in to the sandbox control.
capNote: lines: one row per sentence, and one caption per row. A line of two sentences is two rows with suffixed ids (N01a, N01b) that abut. 'take' is the sentence's span in the narration take; a voiced row starts where its voice starts and lasts at least as long. build.py writes the captions and captions.srt/.vtt from these rows.

audio.retakes: retake-<ID>.m4a beside the take, one sentence each (re-recorded 2026-10-27). scripts/retakes.py trims each, levels it to take 1 and places it, and writes the row's 'source', 'take', 'gainDb' (and 'tempo', at most 1.05, when a sentence needs it to fit). Rerun it when more arrive.
audio.note: scripts/mix.py builds mix.wav (the one sound track, from 0): each row's sentence cut from the take (or its retake) at its 'take' span and placed at the row's start (time shifts only, unless a row has a tempo), the voice chain, the synthesized bed (bedLufs unducked, down by duckDb under speech, which sits it about 20 dB under the voice; lifts at the title's brand and on the end card, in the pauses only), and the cues. Captions are the words spoken; 'script' keeps the written line where they differ. retakeEq matches the retakes' tone to take 1's (measured on N15, N23 and N25 in both: within 0.3 dB an octave band after it).
audio.finalNote: The final cut (the owner, 10/27: #541, then #542): the narration stem at 0.765x (0.9, then 0.85 more; -2.33 dB from rehearsal E) over the whole film. masterGainDb pins rehearsal E's master gain, so nothing normalizes the voice back up to targetLufs; the mix lands under it, as intended. The bed is 0.5 dB lower (bedLufs -27) so it stays about 18-19 dB under the quieter voice, and its ducking is slower (scripts/mix.py: down over 0.8 s, up over 2 s, held through pauses under 1.5 s). The cues are 3 dB louder, with five more on real on-screen actions: three clicks and two page changes.
